PC: Elicits the story and meaning as well as biomedical facts.
ICS: Introduction . . . gives name and clarifies role
Expresses interest in the person as well as the illness
Facilitates patient’s responses verbally and non-verbally (uses encouragement, silence, repetition, paraphrasing, interpretation)
Deals sensitively with embarrassing and disturbing topics and physical pain
Encourages patient to tell his/her own story
Does not interrupt the opening statement
Begins with open-ended questions, moves to closed
Listens attentively, allows patient to complete statements without interruption and leaves space for patient to think before answering or go on after pausing
Uses concise, easily understood questions and comments, not jargon
